phases.name: The First 72 Hours
phases.goal: Don't die. Establish immediate shelter, fire, water, and basic medical assessment. Stabilize any injuries and account for all group members.
phases.summary: By the end of this phase, you should have basic shelter, fire, water access, and a clear assessment of injuries and resources in your immediate area.
criticalActions: Build shelter: Protection from elements; use natural materials or salvage
Start fire: Warmth, water purification, morale, tool making
Secure water: Locate source, boil or treat, establish collection routine
Assess injuries: Triage all group members; treat wounds and stabilize critical cases
Assess group: Count heads, document skills, injuries, morale, resources
Assess surroundings: Map immediate area; identify threats and resources
outcomes: Basic shelter that protects from wind and rain
Reliable fire for warmth, cooking, and water purification
Drinkable water source and collection system
Initial assessment of group health and resources
Mental framework for longer-term survival

phases.name: Stabilization
phases.goal: Establish sustainable camp routines with sanitation, food production, security, and role assignments. Begin reconnaissance for permanent settlement.
phases.summary: By the end of this phase, your camp should feel established with regular patterns, designated roles, sanitation systems, and a scouted location for Phase 2 settlement.
criticalActions: Establish sanitation: Designated latrine area away from water; waste system
Build food routines: Daily foraging/hunting schedule; storage; cooking rotation
Secure perimeter: Fence or warning system; watch posts; security protocol
Assign roles: Leader, scout, water master, fire keeper, cook, medic, defense
Scout for permanent site: Look for arable land, water, defensibility, materials
outcomes: Established camp with regular routines and designated roles
Reliable food sources (foraged, trapped, or hunted)
Clean water and sanitation systems
Basic perimeter security
Identified location for permanent Phase 2 settlement

phases.name: Settlement
phases.goal: Build permanent shelter, establish reliable food production (agriculture + preservation), form governance, begin craft production (soap, candles, medicine).
phases.summary: By the end of this phase, you should have permanent shelter, first crops planted, food preservation systems, governance structure, and basic craft production underway.
criticalActions: Build permanent structures: Main dwelling, storage, workshop; stone or log
Plant crops: Clear fields, prepare soil, plant staples for winter harvest
Preserve food: Smoke houses, root cellars, drying racks; document methods
Establish animal husbandry: Begin with chickens; establish breeding and care routines
Establish governance: Define rules, conflict resolution, resource distribution
Begin soap/candle production: Collect rendered fat; produce soap and candles
Plant medicine garden: Grow medicinal herbs; catalog properties and uses
outcomes: Permanent shelter with multiple buildings (dwelling, storage, workshop)
First successful crop harvest and preservation
Established governance and decision-making structure
Initial livestock (chickens, goats) with breeding records
Basic craft production (soap, candles, medicine) underway

phases.name: Infrastructure
phases.goal: Develop water systems, power generation, grain milling, textile production, communication, organized entertainment, and specialized medical capability.
phases.summary: By the end of this phase, you should have water systems, mechanical power, textile production, long-distance communication, regular culture/entertainment, and trained midwife and dentist.
criticalActions: Dig wells: Establish reliable groundwater access; build pumps or gravity systems
Build water/wind power: Construct water wheel or windmill for mechanical energy
Establish grain milling: Build grist mill; create staple grain processing
Textile production: Set up spinning, weaving, or basic garment production
Build bakehouse: Permanent oven; establish bread production for community
Radio contact: Build transmitter; establish long-distance communication
Regular entertainment: Organize weekly/monthly gatherings, festivals, games
Medical specialists: Train midwife and dentist; establish medical protocols
outcomes: Reliable water distribution system (wells, aqueducts)
Mechanical power source (water wheel or windmill) in operation
Grain milling capability for staple processing
Textile production capability (spinning and weaving)
Long-distance communication (radio) established
Trained midwife and dentist for medical specialization
Regular cultural activities and entertainment

phases.name: Industrial Foundation
phases.goal: Develop metalworking and tool production, formalize education, establish written records, and create economic/trade systems.
phases.summary: By the end of this phase, you should have metalworking capability, widespread education systems, written records and archives, and established trade networks.
criticalActions: Build forge: Establish blacksmith workshop; locate fuel and ore sources
Smelt iron: Produce basic iron from ore; create foundational metal tools
Produce tools: Mass manufacture nails, hinges, brackets, axes, plows
Start school: Formalize education; teach literacy, numeracy, practical skills
Pottery production: Build kiln; produce bricks, tiles, vessels, ceramics
Written records: Begin papermaking; establish archives for laws and knowledge
Establish economy: Create currency/barter system; establish trade networks
outcomes: Functioning blacksmith forge producing tools and hardware
Iron smelting and basic steel production capability
Formal education system for children and skill training
Written archives of laws, medical knowledge, agricultural data
Pottery/ceramics production for vessels and construction
Trade networks with neighboring settlements established

phases.name: Electrification & Beyond
phases.goal: Generate electricity, advance materials and computing capability, improve communication, and systematically reclaim pre-collapse technology and knowledge.
phases.summary: By the end of this phase and beyond, you should have widespread electrical infrastructure, advanced materials, long-distance communication networks, and be well on the path to technological recovery.
criticalActions: Build generator: Water-powered or wind-powered electrical generator
Establish wiring infrastructure: Distribute electricity; develop lighting systems
Telegraph system: Build long-distance electrical communication network
Advanced materials research: Systematic development of better steel and alloys
Establish mechanical computing: Build computational devices for calculations
Transportation systems: Develop railroads, better ships, wheeled vehicles
Long-term planning: Map knowledge recovery; plan technology reinvention
outcomes: Electrical power generation and distribution system
Telegraph or telephone long-distance communication
Advanced materials production (improved steel, glass, ceramics)
Mechanical or electrical computing devices
Transportation infrastructure (roads, bridges, possibly rails)
Systematic recovery of pre-collapse technological knowledge
